name: ttl-expired-row-visible-before-reap
$comment: TTL visibility, as the server actually defines it: expiry is enforced by the background reaper (default sweep 60s), NOT by query-time filtering — so synchronously after seeding, BOTH rows are visible to a collect, including the row whose expiresAt (0) is in the past. The future row uses a fixed 2100-01-01 epoch-ms. This pins that an engine must NOT eagerly filter expired rows at read time (the rust/ts in-memory engines likewise only reap inside tick()). Deletion-by-reaper is async in every engine and is out of corpus scope. Derived from server/src/reaper.rs + query/terminals.rs (no ttl predicate in the read path).
